Months after fleeing their communities over bandit attacks, displaced families in Yabo Local Government Area of Sokoto State say they remain uncertain about where to settle, with their former homes and farmlands no longer accessible to them. They have consequently appealed to the government to provide permanent accommodation and livelihood support to enable them to rebuild their lives after losing their homes and means of survival to insecurity. They made the appeal on Friday during the distribution of dignity kits and other relief materials organised by ActionAid Nigeria, with support from the European Union, at the Yabo Local Government Secretariat. Speaking on behalf of others, displaced resident Mukhtar Umar said farming, which was their major source of livelihood before the attacks, was no longer possible because bandits had taken over their communities and farmlands. “Before now, we used to farm, but where we are now, we cannot do that. Our farms have been taken over by bandits, so we are desperately in need of help,” he said. Umar acknowledged the assistance received from the government and humanitarian organisations but stressed that the displaced families urgently needed decent accommodation and regular food supplies. He appealed for more sustainable interventions to enable them to rebuild their lives. Another beneficiary, Modi Tuita, said displaced residents were experiencing serious hardship after leaving their communities in search of safety. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Similarly, a representative of the displaced women, Hafsat Muhammad, appealed to the government and international organisations to assist them in securing decent homes. Speaking at the event, ActionAid Nigeria’s Deputy Country Director, Suwaiba Dankabo, said the intervention was not merely about distributing relief materials but also about advocating safe housing and improved social protection for displaced persons. Dankabo explained that the dignity kits were designed based on needs identified by beneficiaries, particularly women, and included sanitary pads and other essential items. She disclosed that ActionAid had targeted 300 beneficiaries, with 100 expected to receive the items during the initial distribution, while the remaining beneficiaries would be reached subsequently. On efforts to provide long-term support, Dankabo said the organisation was implementing a three-year partnership programme with the Sokoto State Government under its European Union-supported social protection initiative. Meanwhile, the Vice Chairman of Yabo Local Government, Usman Na’Allah, disclosed that the council had been providing accommodation, foodstuffs and medications to displaced persons. Speaking on behalf of the council chairman, Na’Allah said some displaced families had been accommodated in government-owned properties without paying rent. “At a time, we had about 2,300 persons who came here from neighbouring villages in Shagari Local Government Area. Some of them were accommodated in government properties without collecting a kobo,” he said. He added that the council had appealed to residents to accommodate displaced families where possible, while the local government chairman continued to support them with food and medical assistance. Na’Allah commended ActionAid, the European Union and the federal and state governments for their interventions, urging beneficiaries not to sell the relief materials but to use them for their intended purposes. He also expressed hope that lasting peace would enable the displaced persons to return to their communities and resume their normal lives. The District Head of Yabo, Alhaji Muhammad Sani Bello, commended ActionAid for supporting displaced persons in the area. Animashaun Salman
